title: Naval Topic 1 生词 · 单词卡

cards.ex: Dissatisfaction is the feeling that what you have is not good enough. You want more or you want something better. It is the opposite of being satisfied.
exs: Her dissatisfaction with her old job made her start her own lash studio.
A little dissatisfaction can push you to grow.

src.t: Happiness is being satisfied with what you have. Success comes from dissatisfaction. Is success worth it then?
src.zh: 快乐就是满足于自己拥有的东西。成功来自不满足。那么，成功值得吗？

lg: 心里有个声音一直说：“还不够。”

cards.ex: If something is worth it, the good part is bigger than the cost or the effort. You are glad you did it. People often ask, is it worth it?
exs: The training was expensive, but it was totally worth it.
Waking up early is hard, but it's worth it.

src.t: Happiness is being satisfied with what you have. Success comes from dissatisfaction. Is success worth it then?
src.zh: 快乐就是满足于自己拥有的东西。成功来自不满足。那么，成功值得吗？

lg: 付出的代价，换回来的东西更多。

cards.ex: A statement is something you say or write that tells an idea or a fact. When Naval says that statement, he means a sentence he said before.
exs: That's a strong statement. Do you really believe it?
The salon made a statement about the new prices.

src.t: Oof. I’m not sure that statement is true anymore.
src.zh: 呃。我已经不确定那句话还对不对了。

lg: 把一个想法清清楚楚地“摆出来”。

cards.ex: Highly means very or very much. We use it before some adjectives, like highly contextual or highly recommended. It sounds a little more serious than very.
exs: This lash glue is highly recommended by other artists.
She is a highly skilled lash technician.

src.t: I made that statement a long time ago, and a lot of these things are just notes to myself and they’re highly contextual.
src.zh: 那句话是我很久以前说的，而且很多这类东西只是我写给自己的笔记，非常看当时的情境。

lg: 程度被推到很高的位置。

cards.zh: 取决于情境的；跟上下文有关的
cards.ex: Contextual means it depends on the situation around it. A contextual idea is true in one moment or place, but maybe not in another.
exs: The meaning of a joke is very contextual.
His advice was contextual. It fit his life, not mine.

src.t: I made that statement a long time ago, and a lot of these things are just notes to myself and they’re highly contextual.
src.zh: 那句话是我很久以前说的，而且很多这类东西只是我写给自己的笔记，非常看当时的情境。

lg: 意思要放回当时的“场景”里看。

cards.ex: Complicated means it has many parts and it is hard to understand or explain. It is the opposite of simple.
exs: Volume lashes look simple, but the technique is complicated.
It's complicated. I'll explain it later.

src.t: Happiness is a very complicated topic, but I always like the Socrates story
src.ft: Happiness is a very complicated topic, but I always like the Socrates story where he goes into the marketplace and they show him all these luxuries and fineries and he says, “How many things there are in this world that I do not want,” and that’s a form of freedom, so not wanting something is as good as having it.
src.zh: 快乐是个非常复杂的话题，不过我一直很喜欢苏格拉底的那个故事：他走进集市，人们给他看各种奢侈品和华服美饰，他说：“这世上竟有这么多我不想要的东西啊。”那就是一种自由，所以不想要一样东西，和拥有它一样好。

lg: 线团缠在一起，很难理清。

cards.ex: A marketplace is an open place in a town where people buy and sell things. Today it can also mean any place to buy and sell, like an online marketplace.
exs: We walked around the marketplace and tried some street food.
She sells her lash products on an online marketplace.

src.t: where he goes into the marketplace and they show him all these luxuries and fineries and he says, “How many things there are in this world that I do not want,”
src.ft: Happiness is a very complicated topic, but I always like the Socrates story where he goes into the marketplace and they show him all these luxuries and fineries and he says, “How many things there are in this world that I do not want,” and that’s a form of freedom, so not wanting something is as good as having it.

lg: 大家聚在一起买和卖的地方。

cards.ex: A luxury is something nice and expensive that you enjoy but do not really need. Luxuries is the plural. A day at the spa is a luxury.
exs: For me, a long hot bath is a real luxury.
They live a life of luxury.

src.t: where he goes into the marketplace and they show him all these luxuries and fineries and he says, “How many things there are in this world that I do not want,”

lg: 不是必需，但让人觉得很享受的好东西。

cards.zh: 华服美饰；漂亮的衣服和首饰
cards.ex: Finery means beautiful, expensive clothes and jewelry, the kind you wear to show off. It is a slightly old word. In the story, fineries are fancy things to look rich.
exs: Everyone came to the wedding in their finery.
The queen was dressed in all her finery.

src.t: where he goes into the marketplace and they show him all these luxuries and fineries and he says, “How many things there are in this world that I do not want,”

lg: 穿上最华丽的衣服和首饰去“显摆”。

cards.ex: A form of means one kind or one type of something. When Naval says a form of freedom, he means one way to be free.
exs: Walking is a great form of exercise.
Taking care of yourself is a form of self-respect.

src.t: and that’s a form of freedom, so not wanting something is as good as having it.

lg: 同一类东西里的“其中一种样子”。

cards.ex: As good as means just as good, or almost the same as. Not wanting something is as good as having it means it gives you the same feeling.
exs: After the repair, my phone is as good as new.
The job is as good as done. I just need to send it.

src.t: and that’s a form of freedom, so not wanting something is as good as having it.

lg: 两边放在一起，几乎一样。

cards.ex: To conquer means to win and take control of a place or people, usually in a war. It can also mean to beat a problem or a fear.
exs: Alexander conquered many countries.
She finally conquered her fear of speaking English.

src.t: In the old story with Alexander and Diogenes, Alexander goes out and conquers the world and he meets Diogenes who’s living in a barrel.
src.zh: 在亚历山大和第欧根尼的老故事里，亚历山大出去征服了世界，然后遇到了住在一个木桶里的第欧根尼。

cards.ex: To block means to stand or be in the way, so something cannot get through. If you block my sun, your body stops the sunlight from reaching me.
exs: Your head is blocking the light. Can you move a little?
A big truck was blocking the road.

src.t: Diogenes says “Get out of the way, you’re blocking my sun,”
src.ft: Diogenes says “Get out of the way, you’re blocking my sun,” and Alexander says “Oh how I wish I could be like Diogenes in the next life,” and Diogenes says, “I don’t wish to be Alexander.”
src.zh: 第欧根尼说：“让开，你挡住我的阳光了。”亚历山大说：“唉，我多希望下辈子能像第欧根尼一样。”第欧根尼却说：“我可不想当亚历山大。”

lg: 一块东西挡在路中间，过不去。

cards.ex: To satisfy means to give someone what they need or want, so they feel it is enough. You satisfy your hunger when you eat.
exs: Nothing seems to satisfy him. He always wants more.
This salad won't satisfy me. I need real food.

src.t: So two paths to happiness: one path is success, you get what you want, you satisfy your material needs,
src.ft: So two paths to happiness: one path is success, you get what you want, you satisfy your material needs, or like Diogenes, where you just don’t want it in the first place.
src.zh: 所以通往快乐有两条路：一条是成功，你得到想要的东西，满足你的物质需求，另一条就像第欧根尼那样，你从一开始就不想要它。

lg: 把空的地方填满，让人觉得“够了”。

cards.ex: Material needs are the things you need for your body and daily life, like food, a home, clothes and money. They are things, not feelings.
exs: Once your material needs are met, money matters less.
Work can meet your material needs, but not all your needs.

src.t: So two paths to happiness: one path is success, you get what you want, you satisfy your material needs,
src.ft: So two paths to happiness: one path is success, you get what you want, you satisfy your material needs, or like Diogenes, where you just don’t want it in the first place.
src.zh: 所以通往快乐有两条路：一条是成功，你得到想要的东西，满足你的物质需求，另一条就像第欧根尼那样，你从一开始就不想要它。

lg: 身体和生活需要的“看得见的东西”：吃、住、穿、钱。

cards.zh: 有道理的；站得住脚的；有效的
cards.ex: Valid means it makes sense and has good reasons behind it. A valid idea or point is fair and logical. A valid ticket is one you can still use.
exs: That's a valid point. I didn't think about it.
Is this coupon still valid?

src.t: I’m not sure which one is more valid, and it also depends what you define as success.
src.zh: 我不确定哪条路更站得住，而且这也取决于你怎么定义成功。

cards.ex: Your end goal is the final thing you want to reach, the reason behind all the small steps. Ask yourself, what is the end goal?
exs: My end goal is to open my own lash studio.
Don't forget the end goal: happy clients.

src.t: If the end goal is happiness, then why not cut to the chase and just go straight for it?
src.zh: 如果最终目标是快乐，那为什么不直奔主题，直接去追求快乐呢？

lg: 所有小步骤最后指向的那个终点。

cards.ex: Cut to the chase means skip the slow parts and go straight to the main point. People say it when they want you to stop talking around something.
exs: Let me cut to the chase: we need to raise our prices.
Okay, cut to the chase. What do you want?

src.t: If the end goal is happiness, then why not cut to the chase and just go straight for it?
src.zh: 如果最终目标是快乐，那为什么不直奔主题，直接去追求快乐呢？

lg: 把中间拖拉的部分剪掉，直接跳到重点。
